topic: What Colonel Tom Parker never told Elvis — the secret that controlled his entire career
script: Colonel Tom Parker was not born Tom Parker, and he was never an American citizen. He was born Andreas Cornelis van Kuijk, in Breda, in the Netherlands, in 1909. He entered the United States illegally. He enlisted in the Army under a new name. He never held a U.S. passport. In 1960, his sister back home recognized him in a magazine photograph beside Elvis. Then came the offers. Millions of dollars, from Saudi Arabia, from South America, from promoters across the world, all to bring Elvis to them. Parker turned them down, one after another. Elvis performed outside the United States only in Canada, in 1957. Biographers have long suspected the reason was a manager who could not risk leaving the country. Fans across the world bought his records by the millions. Most of them never saw him on a stage. They only heard the voice, carried home on vinyl.

sources.claim: Parker was born Andreas Cornelis van Kuijk in Breda, Netherlands, on June 26, 1909
Parker was a native of Breda, born 1909 as Andreas van Kuijk
He entered the United States illegally
He enlisted in the U.S. Army under the assumed name Tom Parker
He never held a U.S. passport and was never naturalized as an American citizen
In 1960 his sister Nel Dankers-van Kuijk recognized him in a magazine photo with Elvis
Overseas offers included $5M/$10M from Saudi Arabia and up to $2.5M from South American promoters; Parker declined them
Parker turned down dozens of offers for world tours
Elvis's only concerts outside the U.S. were in Canada in 1957 (Toronto, Ottawa, Vancouver)
Elvis's only foreign concerts were three in Canada in 1957
Biographers/observers suspect his immigration status explains Elvis never touring abroad (speculation, attributed as such)
Elvis's records sold worldwide in the many millions (Guinness: best-selling solo artist)
